data.title: Query immediately returns zero replies after queryable reconnect
data.body:
### Describe the bug

After a queryable disconnects and reconnects, a newly declared querier can immediately return zero replies.

The configured timeout is 10 seconds, but `recv_async()` fails after only a few milliseconds:

The same query works before the disconnection and shortly after the failed call. During the failure, the router receives the querier interest and returns the current queryable declaration, but never receives the query request.

Here's my network topology to reproduce the issue, it may occur in other contexts:

```text
requester (client) → router → responder (client/queryable)
```

- Multicast scouting disabled
- Explicit router endpoint



### To reproduce

Use https://github.com/bdjellabaldebaran/zenoh-queryable-reconnect-repro

Start the router:

```sh
docker run --rm --network host eclipse/zenoh:1.10.0 -l tcp/0.0.0.0:7447
```

Start the provided responder and requester:

```sh
cargo run -- responder
```

```sh
cargo run -- requester
```

Observed output:

```text
before disconnect: reply=pong ...
immediately after reconnect: ZERO REPLIES ... after a few milliseconds
one second later: reply=pong ...
```

### Expected behavior

The query should reach the router or wait for its configured timeout.

### Actual behavior

It immediately completes with zero replies and never reaches the router.

### Possibly related

- [#2204 — `querier.matching_listener` not working after reconnect](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh/issues/2204)
- [#2205 — Fix queryable info update after connection loss](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh/pull/2205)
- [#2516 — `session.get()` immediately returns zero replies](https://github.com/eclipse-zenoh/zenoh/issues/2516)

### Complete logs

The complete router trace is attached here:

[router-trace.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31836419/router-trace.log)

The relevant interval is `12:58:27`–`12:58:38 UTC`.

### Relevant router logs

The first responder (`e88c3da0`) declares the queryable:

```text
2026-09-04T12:58:27.960880Z DEBUG ... src=south:0:client/e88c3da0:2}:declare_queryable ... expr.mapped=repro/service/rpc
2026-09-04T12:58:27.960893Z DEBUG ... register_queryable ... res=repro/service/rpc
```

The requester (`7423bba6`) sends its first query successfully:

```text
2026-09-04T12:58:29.560622Z DEBUG ... src=south:0:client/7423bba6:3}:send_request ... Route query for res repro/service/rpc
2026-09-04T12:58:29.560702Z TRACE ... dirs=[... dst_face ... e88c3da0 ...]
2026-09-04T12:58:29.560716Z TRACE ... Propagate query to south:0:client/e88c3da0:2
2026-09-04T12:58:29.561572Z TRACE ... Route reply for query south:0:client/7423bba6:3:1
```

The responder disconnects and undeclares the queryable:

```text
2026-09-04T12:58:31.962413Z DEBUG ... src=south:0:client/e88c3da0:2}:undeclare_queryable
2026-09-04T12:58:31.962429Z DEBUG ... unregister_queryable ... return=LastUnregistered { res: repro/service/rpc }
2026-09-04T12:58:31.962616Z TRACE ... Received: TransportMessage { body: Close(...) }
```

A new responder connection (`1ea42db7`) declares the same queryable:

```text
2026-09-04T12:58:33.967210Z DEBUG ... New transport opened ... 1ea42db709faea95662245d1b953d5ae
2026-09-04T12:58:33.968543Z DEBUG ... src=south:0:client/1ea42db7:4}:declare_queryable ... expr.mapped=repro/service/rpc
2026-09-04T12:58:33.968562Z DEBUG ... register_queryable ... res=repro/service/rpc
```

Three seconds later, the requester declares its second querier. The router receives the interest and sends the existing queryable declaration:

```text
2026-09-04T12:58:36.564141Z DEBUG ... src=south:0:client/7423bba6:3}:interest{id=2 mode=CurrentFuture opts={K Q} ...}
2026-09-04T12:58:36.564281Z DEBUG ... send_current_queryables ... dst=south:0:client/7423bba6:3
2026-09-04T12:58:36.564385Z TRACE ... Scheduled ... DeclareQueryable ... for transmission to ... 7423bba6
2026-09-04T12:58:36.564443Z TRACE ... Scheduled ... DeclareFinal ... for transmission to ... 7423bba6
```

No `send_request` is received at this time. The requester reports zero replies immediately.

Exactly one second later, another `get()` using the same querier reaches the router and succeeds:

```text
2026-09-04T12:58:37.565388Z DEBUG ... src=south:0:client/7423bba6:3}:send_request ... Route query for res repro/service/rpc
2026-09-04T12:58:37.565408Z DEBUG ... dst=south:0:client/1ea42db7:4 dst.has_queryable=true
2026-09-04T12:58:37.565447Z TRACE ... Propagate query to south:0:client/1ea42db7:4
2026-09-04T12:58:37.565985Z TRACE ... Route reply for query south:0:client/7423bba6:3:2
```

This shows that the failed `get()` never reached the router, while the querier's interest did. After the routing state was refreshed, the next `get()` on the same querier succeeded.

### System info

- Arch linux 
- Zenoh 1.10.0
